crossRefs.note: However Festus answered that Paul should be kept in custody at Caesarea, and that he himself was about to depart…
“Let them therefore”, he said, “that are in power among you go down with me, and if there is anything wrong in the man…
Agrippa said to Paul, “You may speak for yourself.” Then Paul stretched out his hand, and made his defense.
and you are told, and you have heard of it, then you shall inquire diligently. Behold, if it is true, and the thing…
then both the men, between whom the controversy is, shall stand before Yahweh, before the priests and the judges who…
and the judges shall make diligent inquisition; and behold, if the witness is a false witness, and has testified…
He who answers before he hears, that is folly and shame to him.
He who pleads his cause first seems right; until another comes and questions him.
“Does our law judge a man, unless it first hears from him personally and knows what he does?”

people.name: Rome
people.line: Capital city of the Roman Empire

translations.web: I answered them that it is not the custom of the Romans to give up any man to destruction before the accused has met the accusers face to face and has had opportunity to make his defense concerning the matter laid against him.
translations.bsb: I told them that it is not the Roman custom to hand a man over before he has had an opportunity to face his accusers and defend himself against their charges.
translations.kjv: To whom I answered, It is not the manner of the Romans to deliver any man to die, before that he which is accused have the accusers face to face, and have licence to answer for himself concerning the crime laid against him.
translations.asv: To whom I answered, that it is not the custom of the Romans to give up any man, before that the accused have the accusers face to face, and have had opportunity to make his defense concerning the matter laid against him.
